name: Veg Fried Rice

ingredients.name: Spring onion (hara pyaz)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 stalks; whites chopped separately from the greens

ingredients.name: Black pepper powder (kali mirch) (or white pepper)
Salt
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅛ tsp (adjust; soy sauce is already salty)

equipment: Chopping board and a sharp knife
Small bowls to keep each chopped vegetable ready (stir-frying is fast, so everything must be chopped before the flame goes on)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup
Plate for cooling the rice if it is freshly cooked

steps.title: Take 200 g (about 1½ cups) cold cooked rice out of the fridge
steps.text: Take 200 g (about 1½ cups) cold cooked rice out of the fridge
steps.tip: if the rice is freshly cooked, spread it on a plate and chill it for at least 30 minutes first.
steps.visualCue: firm, cold grains that hold together in a clump and look dry on the surface
steps.videoShot: a container of cold rice opened and placed on the counter
steps.watchOut: rice that looks wet or glossy and feels warm will turn sticky in the wok; spread it on a plate and chill it for 30 minutes first.

steps.title: Break up the rice gently with your fingers so the grains separate
steps.text: Break up the rice gently with your fingers so the grains separate
steps.visualCue: loose grains with no lumps that fall apart when you lift a handful
steps.videoShot: fingers crumbling a clump of rice into single grains
steps.watchOut: squeezing or pressing mashes the grains into paste; rub lightly instead, and if a lump stays, wet your fingertips with a few drops of water.

steps.title: Peel and finely chop 3 garlic cloves (6 g)
steps.text: Peel and finely chop 3 garlic cloves (6 g)
steps.visualCue: tiny pieces about the size of a sesame seed
steps.cameraCheck: the chopped garlic on the board
steps.videoShot: knife rocking over the garlic
steps.watchOut: big chunks stay raw and sharp while small ones burn; aim for equal tiny pieces.

steps.title: Peel and finely chop ½ inch ginger (3 g), and finely chop 1 green chilli if using
steps.text: Peel and finely chop ½ inch ginger (3 g), and finely chop 1 green chilli if using
steps.visualCue: two small piles of fine pieces and a sharp, fresh smell
steps.videoShot: ginger sliced into thin strips, then chopped
steps.watchOut: chilli juice stays on your fingers; do not touch your eyes, and wash your hands with soap.

steps.title: Dice ¼ medium onion (30 g) into small squares
steps.text: Dice ¼ medium onion (30 g) into small squares
steps.visualCue: pieces about 1 cm square, all roughly the same size
steps.videoShot: onion cut into small squares
steps.watchOut: uneven pieces cook unevenly (some raw, some burnt); cut them as close to the same size as you can.

steps.title: Chop 2 spring onion stalks, keeping the white part and the green part in separate piles
steps.text: Chop 2 spring onion stalks, keeping the white part and the green part in separate piles
steps.visualCue: a small pile of white rings and a larger pile of green rings
steps.cameraCheck: the two piles side by side
steps.videoShot: knife slicing across the stalks
steps.watchOut: mixing the piles; the greens go in at the very end, and if they cook from the start they turn limp and dull.

steps.title: Peel and finely dice ¼ carrot (30 g)
steps.text: Peel and finely dice ¼ carrot (30 g)
steps.visualCue: small orange cubes about the size of a pea
steps.videoShot: carrot cut into sticks, then into tiny cubes
steps.watchOut: thick carrot cubes stay hard after the quick stir-fry; dice them no bigger than a pea, and cut thin sticks first so the pieces stay even.

steps.title: Thinly slice 5–6 French beans (25 g) after trimming the ends
steps.text: Thinly slice 5–6 French beans (25 g) after trimming the ends
steps.visualCue: thin green rounds
steps.videoShot: a bundle of beans sliced crosswise
steps.watchOut: thick slices stay raw and squeaky; keep them thin, about 3 mm.

steps.title: Finely shred ½ cup cabbage (30 g)
steps.text: Finely shred ½ cup cabbage (30 g)
steps.visualCue: thin pale-green strands
steps.videoShot: knife shredding a cabbage wedge
steps.watchOut: thick cabbage pieces release water in the wok and make the rice soggy; shred thin.

steps.title: Deseed and finely dice ¼ capsicum (25 g)
steps.text: Deseed and finely dice ¼ capsicum (25 g)
steps.visualCue: small green squares with no white seeds
steps.videoShot: capsicum cut into strips, then squares
steps.watchOut: leftover seeds taste bitter and pop out when frying; scrape them out with a spoon.

steps.title: Measure 1½ tsp soy sauce and ½ tsp vinegar into one small cup, and keep ¼ tsp pepper and ⅛ tsp salt beside it
steps.text: Measure 1½ tsp soy sauce and ½ tsp vinegar into one small cup, and keep ¼ tsp pepper and ⅛ tsp salt beside it
steps.tip: line everything up next to the stove in the order you will use it.
steps.visualCue: a small cup of dark liquid next to the pepper and salt
steps.videoShot: soy sauce poured into a small cup
steps.watchOut: forgetting this step; once the wok is hot there is no time to measure, and the rice burns while you hunt for the bottle.

steps.title: Heat the wok on high heat until very hot
steps.text: Heat the wok on high heat until very hot
steps.visualCue: a drop of water sizzles and vanishes in 1–2 seconds; faint smoke may rise
steps.videoShot: water flicked into the wok, evaporating instantly
steps.watchOut: a wok that is only warm steams the food instead of frying it; if the water drop just sits and bubbles slowly, wait another 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add 2 tsp (10 g) oil and swirl it around the wok
steps.text: Add 2 tsp (10 g) oil and swirl it around the wok
steps.visualCue: the oil shimmers and flows thin, coating the sides
steps.videoShot: oil swirled up the sides of the wok
steps.watchOut: oil that smokes heavily and smells acrid is too hot; lift the wok off the flame for 10 seconds, then continue.

steps.title: Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli, and stir-fry
steps.text: Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli, and stir-fry
steps.tip: if the garlic starts to brown fast, lower the flame for a few seconds.
steps.visualCue: a strong garlic smell; the garlic just turns pale gold at the edges
steps.videoShot: garlic sizzling in the oil
steps.watchOut: browned garlic turns bitter within seconds; if it darkens, lower the flame and add the onion straight away to cool the pan.

steps.title: Add the diced onion and the spring onion whites, and stir-fry
steps.text: Add the diced onion and the spring onion whites, and stir-fry
steps.visualCue: the onion turns glossy and slightly translucent but is still crunchy
steps.videoShot: onion tossed with the spatula
steps.watchOut: onion that turns brown and soft is overcooked for this dish; keep it moving and move on at the first glossy look.

steps.title: Add the carrot and beans, and stir-fry on high heat
steps.text: Add the carrot and beans, and stir-fry on high heat
steps.visualCue: brighter colour; the carrot is still crunchy when pressed
steps.cameraCheck: the carrots and beans in the wok
steps.videoShot: vegetables tossed in the wok
steps.watchOut: dull olive-green beans mean they are overcooked; take care to keep tossing and move on when the colours are bright.

steps.title: Add the cabbage and capsicum, and stir-fry
steps.text: Add the cabbage and capsicum, and stir-fry
steps.tip: don't overcook. Indo-Chinese vegetables should still have a bite.
steps.visualCue: the cabbage wilts slightly at the edges; everything is bright and crisp-tender
steps.videoShot: green vegetables added and tossed
steps.watchOut: watery, collapsed vegetables with liquid pooling in the wok mean you cooked them too long or the heat is too low; turn the flame to high and move on to the rice.

steps.title: Add the loosened rice to the wok
steps.text: Add the loosened rice to the wok
steps.visualCue: rice spread over the vegetables in a loose heap
steps.cameraCheck: the rice on top of the vegetables
steps.videoShot: rice tipped into the wok
steps.watchOut: dumping in rice that was left in lumps; break any lump on the spot with the spatula edge.

steps.title: Toss and fold the rice with the vegetables on high heat, spreading it out and pressing any lumps
steps.text: Toss and fold the rice with the vegetables on high heat, spreading it out and pressing any lumps
steps.visualCue: the rice is hot right through, grains jump separately and you hear a light crackle
steps.cameraCheck: the rice and vegetables mixed evenly
steps.videoShot: spatula folding the rice from the bottom
steps.watchOut: a sticky, clumped base means the rice was warm or the heat was low; keep tossing on high heat and press the clumps flat against the wok to break them.

steps.title: Pour the soy sauce and vinegar mix around the hot edge of the wok, not straight onto the rice
steps.text: Pour the soy sauce and vinegar mix around the hot edge of the wok, not straight onto the rice
steps.tip: hitting the hot metal caramelises the sauce a little, which gives the "restaurant" smoky taste.
steps.visualCue: a loud sizzle and a smoky, savoury smell
steps.cameraCheck: the sauce hitting the side of the wok
steps.videoShot: sauce drizzled down the side, sizzling
steps.watchOut: pouring in the middle makes dark wet patches and soggy rice; if that happens, toss quickly on high heat until the patches dry.

steps.title: Add ¼ tsp pepper, ⅛ tsp salt and a pinch of sugar (optional), and toss
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp pepper, ⅛ tsp salt and a pinch of sugar (optional), and toss
steps.tip: taste a few grains before adding salt. Soy sauce brands vary a lot in saltiness.
steps.visualCue: the rice turns an even light-brown colour with no white patches
steps.videoShot: rice tossed until evenly brown
steps.watchOut: over-salting, because soy sauce is already salty; taste a few grains first, and rescue salty rice with a squeeze of lemon and a handful of plain rice.

steps.title: Add the spring onion greens, toss for 15 seconds, and turn off the flame
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss for 15 seconds, and turn off the flame
steps.visualCue: bright green flecks throughout
steps.cameraCheck: the finished rice in the wok
steps.videoShot: green spring onion scattered and tossed in
steps.watchOut: leaving the flame on; the greens turn grey and limp within a minute, so switch off straight after tossing.

steps.title: Transfer to a plate and serve immediately
steps.text: Transfer to a plate and serve immediately
steps.visualCue: separate glossy grains with colourful vegetables and steam rising
steps.videoShot: a mound of fried rice on a plate with steam rising (hero shot)
steps.watchOut: leaving the rice in the hot wok; it keeps cooking and the base sticks, so plate it at once.

reasons: the home version uses only 2 tsp oil, about 175 g of mixed vegetables and moderate soy sauce, with no frying beyond a quick stir-fry. It is still mainly refined white rice with only about 8 g protein, so it is filling but not balanced on its own. Restaurant and street versions typically use 2–3 tbsp oil, often add MSG (ajinomoto), use much more soy sauce and salt, and contain far fewer vegetables relative to rice.

researchRating.basis: veg fried rice is one of the most-ordered and most-cooked Indo-Chinese dishes in India, and the top recipe pages still show near-perfect ratings from hundreds of readers. It loses a little because many people see it as a side for Manchurian or chilli dishes rather than a standout dish on its own, and home versions are often described as "not as smoky as the restaurant".

storage: Fridge: cool it quickly (within 1 hour of cooking) and keep it in an airtight container for up to 1 day, at most 2. Cooked rice left at room temperature can grow *Bacillus cereus*, so do not leave it out for long. Freezer: possible for up to 1 month in a flat freezer bag, though the vegetables lose some crunch. Reheating: stir-fry in a hot pan with 1 tsp water or oil for 2–3 minutes until steaming hot all the way through, or microwave covered with a sprinkle of water for 1.5–2 min, stirring halfway. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: make fried-rice "Schezwan arancini" (rice tikkis). Mash about 1 cup leftover fried rice with 2 tbsp grated paneer, 1 tbsp cornflour and ½ tsp Schezwan sauce, shape into small balls or patties, and shallow-fry or air-fry until crisp. Serve with ketchup or mint chutney.
burnOff: Running: about 5.6 km at about 70 kcal per km. Walking: about 8 km at a brisk pace (est.), using about 50 kcal per km.

navratri.reason: it is built on rice (a grain) and uses onion, garlic and soy sauce, none of which fit the most common vrat rule set (assumption: grains and onion/garlic avoided)

ekadashi.reason: rice is avoided on Ekadashi in most families (assumption), and onion and garlic are used

jain.reason: drop onion, garlic, fresh ginger, carrot and spring onion; use capsicum, beans, cabbage and hing (see Jain variant)

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; it is carb-heavy with only about 8 g protein and about 750 mg sodium (est.), so for sehri add tofu or paneer-free protein such as boiled chickpeas on the side and cut the soy sauce

jain.reason: drop onion 30 g, garlic 6 g, fresh ginger 3 g, carrot 30 g and spring onion 20 g (roots and alliums, Patch 05); build flavour on capsicum, beans, cabbage, green chilli and a pinch of hing (see Jain variant)

vegan.reason: no dairy, ghee, egg, honey, meat or fish in the recipe (oil, vegetables and rice only)

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian recipe with no meat or egg

sattvik.reason: skip onion, garlic and spring onion (all alliums); fresh ginger can stay (see Sattvik variant)

glutenFree.reason: ordinary soy sauce is usually brewed with wheat; use a soy sauce or tamari labelled gluten-free (see Gluten-free variant)

dairyFree.reason: no milk, ghee, butter or paneer in the recipe

variants.reason: main recipe already vegan (no dairy, egg, honey or ghee).
as a separate variant — the main recipe already uses only 2 tsp oil; section 7 gives the healthier swaps.
